How it works — the buttons in order

Two lanes: plan-level (four buttons, independent) and shift-level (per-shift after allocation). Blue = primary action; amber = brand action; outline = secondary.

Figure 1. Plan-level vs shift-level — the four plan-level buttons act on a plan but don't change its status; the act of allocating IS the approval. The shift-level row only appears once items become shifts.

Then the agent loop fires

Once a shift is dispatched, the rest of the cycle runs without you. Each lane is one actor; arrows show the handover.

Figure 2. One full loop from plan to signed-off tests, mirrored to Slack and Excel.

VCL PMO · Auto plan-review (proposed)page 04 · 28 may 2026

The auto plan-review loop

Direct from Tanuj's hand-written page-4 annotation on the v4 review. This is the design SHIFT-0002 (Codex) is now writing up as a spec.

Figure 3. The six-step auto-review loop. Tanuj's rough plan → agent drafts → Slack approval → bulk-allocate. After step 6, control returns to Figure 1 (Execute via n8n → Start → Complete).

What changes in /app/pmo

  • Inbox becomes the queue. The Inbox tab gets filtered to "needs Tanuj" — plans waiting for approval, shifts waiting for UAT sign-off, blocked requirements. Today it shows too much.
  • New Plan stays the entry point. Tanuj writes a one-line direction in /app/pmo (same modal as today) — no need to leave for Slack.
  • The agent drafts. Codex (default) or Claude (fallback when Codex is at quota) reads the rough plan + project context + the last 5 approved plans on the same project, expands the items, hints assignees.
  • The PDF lands in Slack. Same Send PDF to Slack button — but now with an "Approve all to Claude / Codex / Human" Block-Kit button below the file.
  • One click bulk-allocates. The button calls slack_approve_plan(plan_id, allocate_to) which delegates to the existing allocate_plan_items and stamps approved_by + approved_at.

What stays the same

  • You can still allocate manually in /app/pmo whenever you want. The auto-loop is an option, not a replacement.
  • Execute via n8n + Complete are unchanged.
  • UAT/OAT records auto-create on allocation, same as today.

VCL PMO · Your questions, answeredpage 05 · 28 may 2026

Your review questions, answered

All seven annotations from the v4 reMarkable review (archived at briefs/review/2026-05-28_status_report_v4_annotated.pdf).
Q1. How do we install the Slack bot? See the separate one-page setup card (VCL-PMO_slack_bot_setup_card.pdf). Five steps: create app → add chat:write + files:write scopes → install → invite to #ai-pmo-plans → drop the xoxb-… token into Frappe Cloud's site_config via bench set-config. About 10 minutes.
Q2. What about new projects? Today the SPA has no "New Project" button — you have to use the bare Desk form at /app/pmo-project/new. Codex is adding a + New Project button to the portfolio toolbar (next to "New Requirement"), wired to a new create_project API. Codex Item B in the review-response brief.
Q3. Who approves new plans? Today: nothing. A new Plan sits at status=Draft until you click "Allocate selected to …" — the act of allocating IS the approval. Auto-review (Figure 3 above, SHIFT-0002) introduces a Slack-based approval button so you can approve without opening /app/pmo.
Q4. How are Send PDF / Allocate / Execute via n8n linked? They're not — they're independent. Send PDF renders + posts and does NOT change plan state. Allocate promotes ticked items into Shifts (status = Allocated). Execute via n8n is per-shift, fires the agent webhook. Figure 1 on page 3 has been split into plan-level vs shift-level lanes to make this obvious.
Q5. What does the agent do, and how does it fire up? (1) dispatch_shift(shift_id) reads pmo_n8n_dispatch_url from site_config; (2) POSTs the shift payload to n8n; (3) n8n routes by assigned_to (claude / codex) — currently designed to trigger a CLI runner on the dev machine; (4) the agent works, commits, then POSTs back to /api/method/.../complete_shift with output notes + UAT/OAT results; (5) ERPNext flips status → Done, stamps actual_end, logs the UAT/OAT runs. The n8n routing layer is the gap to close.
Q6. The plan-review flow you sketched. That's SHIFT-0002 — Codex's allocated planning shift. Captured exactly as you wrote it, drawn as Figure 3 above. Codex is finishing the spec (briefs/2026-05-28_SCHEDULED_PLAN_REVIEW_SPEC.md) covering: scheduler trigger, capacity probe (pmo_codex_available site_config flag), reviewer payload, Slack-Block-Kit approval surface, action on approve, failure modes.
Q7. Inbox first-page UX. Agreed — Inbox is too noisy. Codex is filtering Inbox to "needs Tanuj" only: plans waiting for allocation, shifts waiting for UAT sign-off, blocked requirements, plan reviews pending (once SHIFT-0002 ships). Codex Item C in the review-response brief.

VCL PMO · Architecturepage 06 · 28 may 2026

Where each piece lives

We deliberately do not try to put everything in one tool. Two anchors: ERPNext is the operational source of truth, Slack + Excel are downstream review surfaces that already work for the team.

Figure 3. One source of truth, two downstream review surfaces. No reverse writes from Slack or Excel back into ERPNext.

What that means in practice

  • You edit in ERPNext. Everything else mirrors automatically.
  • Slack is for reading and annotating. Plans land there as PDFs; nothing in Slack writes back.
  • Excel is for the monthly slice. n8n writes a workbook per project on the share; you never edit it directly.
  • Agents talk to ERPNext directly via whitelisted API methods. n8n is the routing layer, not a data store.

Rules of use

  • Blue is primary. Not navy-black. Not orange-amber. Buttons, links, table headers — all VCL Blue #2B3990.
  • Sage is the brand accent. Logo mark, user-pill avatar, active nav indicator. NOT for status colour.
  • Green is for money + complete. Pricing figures and "Done" — never use blue for these.
  • Amber replaces red for most warnings. Red is restricted to system errors and 90+ day AR overdue.
  • Typography: Manrope (UI), JetBrains Mono (IDs, code). Embedded as base64 in this PDF; no CDN.
